01 / THE QUESTION

What needed to work?

A signal reading alone does not explain where coverage breaks down. A useful survey needs position, signal variability, and a way to check its predictions.

A macOS survey platform connecting CoreWLAN measurements to calibrated plans, mapping, diagnostics, and exports.

SAMPLE SURVEY

03 / THE ENGINEERING

The decision behind it.

Keep measured samples separate from interpolated cells. IDW and RBF estimate between observations; neither is a model of the building’s walls.

  1. 01CoreWLAN measurements
  2. 02Authenticated survey
  3. 03IDW / RBF mapping
  4. 04Analysis & exports
  • Calibrated floor plans and authenticated survey sessions using real laptop measurements.
  • Five-sample RSSI collection, IDW/RBF coverage heatmaps, and channel-overlap analysis.
  • ICMP diagnostics and internet throughput testing.
  • Spatial cross-validation, before/after survey comparisons, and CSV, JSON, and PDF exports with measured and simulated data clearly labeled.

04 / THE EVIDENCE

What the work demonstrates.

Positioned readings become a map you can inspect and compare. The preview uses synthetic samples; field accuracy requires real survey data.

The implementation collects five samples per point, generates coverage maps, and supports checkpoint evaluation and before/after comparisons.

BOUNDARY OF THE EVIDENCE

Field accuracy needs actual survey and checkpoint readings. The portfolio interaction uses sample values.

05 / THE BOUNDARIES

What I can stand behind.

Field accuracy needs actual survey and checkpoint readings. The portfolio interaction uses sample values.

Building something useful means being precise about what it does, what has been checked, and what still needs to be tested.
